newsitem.title: POLAND: Strong dollar weakens Polish zloty, depos inch up.
newsitem.headline: Strong dollar weakens Polish zloty, depos inch up.

text.p: The Polish zloty eased against the basket of currencies on the back of a light dollar-buying trend sparked a strong showing of the U.S. unit in European trade on Monday, dealers said.
The dollar held above crucial support levels of 1.4910 marks and Polish banks began to buy the U.S. currency in anticipation of its gains, which topped around 1.4960 marks.
"A slight dollar-buying trend developed as the dollar rebounded from support levels at above 1.49 marks," said Jan Mieczkowski, treasurer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA.
The zloty closed at 1.66/1.61 percent from the trading band centre, weaker than Friday's close at 1.75/1.70 percent.
It was at 2.7610/25 to the dollar, down from Friday's 2.7503/15 and at 1.8510/18 to the mark, up from 1.8514/23.
On the money market, one-day deposit rates inched up despite a 300 million zloty net inflow into the system as banks struggled to regain liquidity after a week-long shortage.
Overnight rates closed at 19.15/19.35 percent, up from Friday's 18.00/19.30 percent and tommorow/next at 19.20/19.40 percent, just down from opening but up from 19.50/19.30 percent last week.
The money market's tightness pulled up the 14-day reverse repo rate by 0.05 point on Monday to 19.10 percent.

The average yield of the benchmark 52-week paper inched up 0.03 point to 19.42 percent at the treasury's 700 million zloty primary auction, but yields of all other bills fell at the tender under weight of 1.98 billion zlotys worth of bids.
The average yield of the 26-week T-bill fell 0.17 point from last week's auction to 19.11 percent and the 13-week paper by 0.13 point to 18.60 percent.
